reviewFindings: Owned cursor cleanup finishes before readStatistics invokes the native six-counter observation; api.closeNamespace is in the following finally block and is attempted even when observation or snapshot allocation fails.

Final fallback snapshot is preinitialized within the factory-owned construction cleanup boundary. IOException, OOME and invalid array length/negative counters/heap bounds are optional omissions with empty values, never a validated counter claim.
The omission stores only a capped exception class name, never the throwable message. Even omission construction failure falls back to the preallocated bounded generic snapshot.

The original native post-advance failure remains the service failure, with cleanup failures tracked independently; optional counter exceptions are not substituted for it and cannot authorize cursor retries.

The synchronized backend closes only its namespace, records finalStatistics before releasing it, and returns that immutable final snapshot on subsequent calls without native calls. Final values use a privately created map of immutable Longs; native source-array mutation and attempted map modification cannot alter the snapshot.

Normal authenticated peer EOF and explicit owner close both retain final counter evidence, close owned cursor/namespace once, and leave the normal operation successful when only optional statistics fail.

Diagnostic descriptor labels CURRENT versus final capture and omissions, and explicitly scopes heap values to the observation before namespace free. Statistics are entry metadata/core owned heap, not total filesystem calls, process RSS or device memory.

Admission, six external activation gates, runtime identity, resolved-path authority, credential handoff, ordinary native error poisoning and cleanup ownership are unchanged in the authenticated two-file delta.
